// A module whose DATA holds the word `from` as a string literal, so
// `importClosure` can be driven over the shape that once made it refuse a file
// for importing something nobody wrote.
//
// THE DEFECT THIS PINS, DRIVEN RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. The walker matched
// `from` followed by a quote, and in `"from", "why"` the literal's own closing
// quote served as the specifier's opening one - so it read a specifier of
// `", "` (or `",\n  "` when the array is wrapped) and refused
// `tools/stripboard/exemptions-model.ts`, whose `ENTRY_KEYS` names the fields
// of a recorded exemption and one of those fields is `from`. The fix requires
// the keyword to be preceded by whitespace or `}`, which every real import and
// re-export is.
//
// ITS EXTENSION IS `.ts.txt` for the reason `./bare-specifier-importer.ts.txt`
// gives: the walker reads a file's text and never its extension.
import { closureSha256 } from "../../lib/import-closure.ts"

// Both spellings: wrapped, as a formatter leaves a long array, and on one line.
export const ENTRY_KEYS = [
  "id",
  "from",
  "why",
]

export const LIST_KEYS = ["from", "doesNotExcuse", "consultedBy"]

export const hash = closureSha256
